cards.title: Lists hold many values
cards.body: A list keeps values in order inside square brackets. `nums[0]` is the first item.

cards.title: Reading a line of numbers
cards.body: `input().split()` gives a list of text pieces. `map(int, ...)` turns each into a number and `list()` collects them.

cards.title: sum() adds a list
cards.body: `sum(nums)` adds up every number in the list.

cards.title: Spot the bug
cards.body: It should print the last item, 15, but crashes with an `IndexError`. Which line is wrong?

bug.fix: The first item is `nums[0]`, so 15 is `nums[2]` (or `nums[-1]`). There is no `nums[3]`.

exercise.prompt: Read whole numbers on one line, separated by spaces, and print their total.
exercise.starterCode:
nums = list(map(int, input().split()))
# print the total of nums
